rationale: String Confirmation Day materially changed the observable 2026 application graph: 152 replacement selections, nine withdrawals and a reduction in public identical-string contention from 263/891 at Reveal Day to 226/705. The same-day ICANN announcement exposes a reproducible four-application aggregate/publication gap that must be preserved as an unresolved finding rather than normalized away.
evidenceLimitations: ICANN's 17 November announcement aggregates do not fully reconcile with the public APS export and public contention CSV.

Statistics at 18:09 and 18:39 UTC reported 1,615 total, 1,606 active and nine withdrawn. The arithmetic 1,615 minus nine equals 1,606; the announcement gives 1,610. This establishes an aggregate difference, not four missing records.

The repeated four-unit marginal differences do not establish four missing applications, a shared application profile or an administrative cause. A counting/editorial error, scope difference or publication timing issue remains possible.
.wdo remains a separate known administrative-check case absent from the public Applications listing.
The historical 1,616 paid-to-proceed figure of 22 September and the 1,615 Reveal Day figure remain a distinct unresolved discrepancy.
RR1 and RR2 remain immutable; this candidate has no DOI until archival verification completes.

Later Statistics at 20:09 UTC report 1,605 Active and ten Withdrawn, while the export rechecked at 20:38 UTC remains byte-identical with 1,605 Active and nine Withdrawn public records. These asynchronous observations are separate from the frozen 18:30 snapshot and do not identify the tenth withdrawal.
